note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

precepts.why:
Ishmael “dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.” He learned the skills of combat and war, according to his nature, and that nature was spoken before he was born. The angel of the Lord told Hagar, “thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the Lord hath heard thy affliction. And he will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.”

The word over his lineage stands: a wild people, his hand against every man and every man’s hand against him, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren in the Middle East. He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and “his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.”

The dragons have the upper hand, remembering their nature. Let's get their nature. “And the angel of the Lord said unto her,” To Hagar. “Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael;” Ishmaelite, in the Zondervan Bible dictionary: the word is used in the Old Testament in a wider sense, referring to the nomadic tribes of northern Arabia generally, and all Arabs, following Muhammad's example, that is Islam, claim descent from Ishmael. So they know who they are. “because the Lord hath heard thy affliction.” That is what Ishmael means: affliction heard.

“And he will be a wild man;” The Bible says the descendants of Ishmael shall be wild. How wild? They are willing to strap C4 on their bodies, and not just the men: now they have the women doing it, children doing it, blowing everything to hell and back. That is how wild they are. You better run the hell out of there. “his hand will be against every man,” See that: his hand will be against every man. Black people in America think, oh, this is my friend Habib. No, no: they are for one cause, and they are willing to sacrifice everybody for their religion. “and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.” That is that area they call the Middle East. So in 2 Esdras 15:30, as the wild boars of the wood: there are the Arabs again, there is Ishmael again.

moments.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: The angel found Hagar fleeing from Sarai and told her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands; Sarah was hard on her because she was disrespectful. I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude: that goes into Ishmael. Look how many Arabs there are all over the world today; that is prophecy.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: This is before chapter 21, while the child was still in her womb: thou shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael, because the Lord hath heard thy affliction. Ishmael means affliction heard, and his name is important to future prophecy.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: And he will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man's hand against him. Why? Because he was a warrior, skillful with the bow. That happened back then, but it is also prophetic; it is future prophecy concerning Ishmael, concerning the Arabs. And he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Hagar was Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, from the servants Pharaoh gave in Genesis 12:16.
Sarai, restrained from bearing, gave her maid to Abram that she might obtain children by her.
Sarai laid the wrong on Abram, and Abram answered, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand. He did not say my wife; he had no attachment to Hagar. His sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives.
When Hagar conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes. Hagar got high minded; she stopped submitting because she carried Abram's child.
Abram kept the laws of the Most High. Do not use this account to justify taking multiple wives; the purpose here was the promised inheritance, and Sarai dealt with her maid as mistress over her.
The angel of the Lord found Hagar by the fountain in the way to Shur and sent her back: Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands. Humble yourself and go back.
Ishmael would be a wild man, his hand against every man and every man's hand against him, and he would dwell in the presence of all his brethren.
They dwell in the presence of all their brethren to this day, nation beside nation through that whole region.

Abram was fourscore and six years old, eighty six, when Hagar bare Ishmael. Ishmael was Abram's firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael; the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel.
